title: The tool bar claims more room than it draws once a measurement exists
goal: With a measurement in the document and a narrow window, the floating tool bar still looks like one row but reports itself about four times taller. If that taller area is really there, it would quietly swallow clicks on the lower part of the picture, which is exactly where you often want to measure. Find out whether it is real, and if it is, stop it.
notes: Observed 2026-08-23 with a temporary env-gated geometry probe while fixing the measure hint chip. onGeometryChange on the GlassEffectContainer wrapping `toolbar` in EditorView reported h 48 in every state EXCEPT after EditorState.addMeasure in a 700pt-wide window, where it settled at h 200 with the bottom still pinned (544..744 in a 760pt canvas), i.e. it grew upward. Most likely benign: GlassEffectContainer reserves a morph region around newly inserted glass shapes, and the measureCountPill appears exactly then. Verify by hit-testing, not by reading frames: the container has no allowsHitTesting(false). Cannot affect the measure hint chip (that only shows while the document holds no measurements).
acceptance: Clicking anywhere in the bottom strip of the picture, just above the tool bar, reaches the picture and not the bar
The tool bar occupies only the row it draws, in a narrow window and a wide one, with and without measurements in the document
Whatever is found is written down, including the case where the answer is that nothing is wrong

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the report reads a FRAME, and a frame is not a click. GlassEffectContainer reserves a morph region around glass shapes, so a tall frame with no hit-testable content in it swallows nothing. Decided to answer by hit-testing and to build nothing unless a click actually goes missing.

Offscreen harness first (temp/toolbar-hittest2.swift): canvas as an NSViewRepresentable, AppKit hitTest sweep, with controls proving the method discriminates (no overlay: canvas owns everything; a solid 200pt overlay: canvas loses exactly 200pt). Result: a GlassEffectContainer forced to 200pt tall, and the measuring .background(GeometryReader{Color.clear}), claim nothing. Only the controls claim.

Then the real app, which is the evidence that counts. Temporary env-gated probe (PHOTONZ_HITTEST_PROBE=1) in the probe bundle: sweeps the live editor window with AppKit hit tests, classifying every point as owned by CanvasNSView or taken. Five states: narrow 700x760 with no measurement, with the Measure tool active, with one measurement, with two, and wide 1400x900. In EVERY state the only rows the canvas loses are y=26..54 off the canvas bottom. Nothing above y=58 is ever taken. THE REPORTED PROBLEM IS NOT REAL: the tall frame costs no clicks.

The sweep found the opposite defect. EditorChromeLayout says the bar is 48pt of glass around a 28pt control row; the claimed band was 28pt, so the 10pt glass rim above and below the controls was passing clicks THROUGH to the picture. With Measure active, aiming a few points high at a tool started a measurement on the image instead of picking the tool. Fixed: .contentShape(.capsule) on the tools capsule, the compact tools capsule, the color capsule and the zoom capsule, so each absorbs clicks on the whole capsule it draws.

Verified the fix on the real app with the same probe: the claimed band becomes y=18..62 (the drawn capsule, 16..64), with the capsule's rounded ends visible in the data (leftmost claim 250 at y=18, 234 at mid-height), and still nothing above y=62 in any of the five states. Also posted real clicks at the tool row inside the app: clicking across the bar still switches the tool (select -> rectSelect -> arrow), so the content shape did not steal the controls' own hits.

Found on the way, filed as the-tool-bar-runs-off-both-edges-of-the-picture: at 700x760 with the inspector docked the canvas is 435pt and the bar's claim runs from x=2 to the canvas edge, i.e. the bar is wider than the picture, clipped visually but not for input.
Shared-code note: EditorView is shared, so both releases get this fix. It is a defect fix, not a design difference, so it does not belong behind a next-scoped flag.
Cleanup: temporary probe (Sources/Photonz/DevHitTestProbe.swift, its AppDelegate hook, CanvasNSView.debugActiveTool) removed. swift build clean, Scripts/test.sh green (1061 tests). Probe app quit.

Hit-tested the live app in five states: the reported tall click blocker does not exist, the bar only ever claims the band it draws. The sweep found the reverse defect instead, the 10pt glass rim above and below the controls passed clicks through to the picture, so the tools, compact tools, color and zoom capsules now carry .contentShape(.capsule). Verified with the same in-app hit-test sweep plus real clicks that still switch tools. Audit: queue/audits/2026-08-24-toolbar-hit-area.json. Follow-up filed: the-tool-bar-runs-off-both-edges-of-the-picture.
